new.analysis:
Week one was a sound restart, and the data shows your shin handled it. All three sessions stayed at 0 out of 10 pain, the shin was quiet afterwards, and average heart rate sat around 121 to 123 bpm, well under your 178 bpm ceiling.

Week one counts as the first of the four pain-free weeks in a row you need before any intervals, hills or strides. A pain-free week means every run stayed at 0 out of 10 and the shin was quiet the next morning. Any pain, even if it settles, starts the count again.

Next week's total time rises by about 7 percent, which keeps you inside the 10 percent limit for a return. I kept the running blocks at 2 minutes rather than lengthening them. The export shows only session totals, so I cannot confirm the block lengths you used, and a longer block could be a bigger jump than intended.

| | Sep 7 – 13 | Sep 14 – 20 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sessions | 3 | 3 |
| Time per session | about 15 min | 16 min |
| Total time | 45 min | 48 min |

The calf and hip routine stays at two sessions, on Tue and Fri, since you already complete it reliably and it fits between runs. Thu and Sun are full rest days, so each run has a day before and after it. If the shin aches during a run, stop. If pain stays at 3 out of 10 or below and settles by the next morning, take the next small step. If it goes above 3 out of 10 during a run, or is worse the next morning, repeat this week's session instead.
